transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Friday, October 9. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. 'Drunk men around me': Assam student's last video from train before she went missing. Himashri Boro, a 20-year-old student from Assam, was travelling alone after a dance competition. She felt unsafe in her train compartment due to inebriated men surrounding her and reached out to her family. Contact was lost between 2:30am and 3:00am, prompting her family to alert the railway authorities. Her body was later discovered near railway tracks in Andhra Pradesh's Srikakulam district. Anthropic updates Claude policy, may 'ban' users who are abusive or cruel to its AI. Anthropic has unveiled vital changes to its acceptable usage policy for the AI model Claude. These refined guidelines primarily aim to combat various forms of abuse directed at the AI and address new threats. Among the prohibitions are actions such as deception, interference with elections, and attempts to weaponize the AI. Furthermore, human supervision is now a mandatory requirement for all AI applications, ensuring safety and accountability in technology. Starlink entry row: Is Ambani the real boss of India, asks Elon Musk. Elon Musk has raised concerns about regulatory obstacles facing Starlink's introduction in India. He claimed influential figures might be hindering the process and questioned if Ambani controls the situation. In response, India's government reaffirmed its fair and non-discriminatory approach, rejecting Musk's allegations. Other companies like Reliance Jio and Eutelsat OneWeb are also vying for approval to offer satellite services. 'This is emergency': 10,000 detained ahead of Delhi's Jantar Mantar stir, says CJP. The Cockroach Janta Party's planned protest in Delhi has faced significant opposition, leading to numerous detentions across the country. Over 10,000 individuals, including students, were detained ahead of the October 10 demonstration. CJP leaders have criticized the government's restrictions on public gatherings while demanding accountability for alleged electoral irregularities. As civil society groups rally in support, the party persists in organizing the protest. US suspends Microsoft from Green Card programme, here is what the company has to say. The US has suspended Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM), freezing new and pending Green Card applications for its foreign workers. Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of abusing the H-1B and PERM system to replace laid-off American workers. Microsoft says 80 percent of its roughly 6,000 H-1B filings last fiscal year were for existing employees, and that it pays H-1B staff the same as others doing comparable work. Flydubai cockpit attack: Israel to honour Capt Smit with top civilian bravery award. Israel has announced that Captain Smit Machchhar will receive a prestigious Presidential Award for his bravery. He prevented a potential aviation disaster aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073 by acting decisively against a radicalized co-pilot. During the incident, six Israeli passengers displayed great courage in assisting Machchhar and foiling the hijack attempt. This heroic act has led to a broader investigation into the circumstances of the attack. Woman claims 2.5 acres was ancestral after stepmother sold it; why HC rejected plea. The Madras High Court held that the property was not ancestral but self-acquired. As a result, under Hindu law, the man and his mother were legally entitled to execute the gift settlement deed in favour of the man's second wife, who could subsequently sell the property. BCCI Centre of Excellence treated 32 top cricketers last year. The BCCI's Centre of Excellence reported a rise in rehabilitated players, with 32 men undergoing treatment recently. A budget increase of nearly rupees 35 crore was allocated for injury management and rehabilitation. Soft-tissue injuries predominated among the cases, with notable players affected. Communication issues between Team India and the CoE's Sports Science Medicine team have been highlighted. Non-cyclist CEO rides 2,000 miles in 12 days, raises $766K for 70 causes. Matt King, CEO of Gobundance, trained for five and a half months before cycling nearly 2,000 miles from Mexico to Canada in 12 days. Along the journey, King and his team raised more than $766,000 and distributed funds to over 70 individuals and organisations, supporting families and communities facing financial hardships. Swift, Kelce called 'absentee' owners over $5.35M Ohio mansion plan. Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are facing objections from neighbours over security fencing and landscaping at their $5.35 million Ohio mansion. Residents have raised concerns about a shared sewer line, wildlife safety and privacy. The couple's representatives say they scaled back the fence and preserved neighbour access, while the board requested revisions to shoreline tree plans.
